text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 decode latency spike detected on prod-us-west (streaming). metric: decode.p99=2.7s (SLO >1.2s). Auto-paging threshold breached.
ava_oncall: on it. seeing correlated streaming stalls in logs, sessions piling up.
ava_oncall: @liam_infra can you confirm whether the TRT8 kernel rollout hit us in us-west earlier? I saw deploy window ~02:15UTC.
liam_infra: yes, kernel image v4.19-trt8+flashattn pushed to prod us-west at 02:12UTC as part of the infra batch. only ~40% of pool rolled before autoscaler paused.
liam_infra: digging into node-level logs now.
rachel_runtime: I’m seeing a waveform of p95 -> p99 divergence at ~02:20UTC on decode, streaming sessions show repeated stalls at KV cache lookup. stack traces point to new HLO/compile path in the runtime.
dario_sre: any customer-facing errors? @sofia_support?
sofia_support: Support queue: 3 customers reported long responses and a streaming timeout at ~02:25UTC. One is a priority enterprise customer (cust-zenith). They've throttled traffic but still see tail blips.
mike_eng: I have a repro trace from a small internal load test pinned to the new kernel. capture attached: ```
# tail of runtime log
[02:23:41] decode: waiting for kv-cache lock
[02:23:41] decode: paging candidate triggered, alloc failure
[02:23:41] runtime: fallback to single-stream path
[02:23:42] decode: complete 1.9s
```
ava_oncall: ok. hypothesis: new TRT/FlashAttention kernels + compiler flags changed codegen causing more paging / cache invalidations under streaming patterns. gives higher tail latency.
liam_infra: confirmed dmesg shows elevated page reclaim events and a few OOM_killer candidates that recover immediately (no kills). kernel vm tuning looks different from previous baseline.
rachel_runtime: rolling canary back gave <10% p99 improvement in a quick test on a node. full rollback would need draining nodes with v4.19-trt8 and replacing with v4.19-stable.
dario_sre: mitigation options: 1) rollback kernel image (slow), 2) toggle compiler flag XLA_DEFER=0 (if runtime supports), 3) route heavy streaming traffic to eu region (failover), 4) enable runtime-level prefix caching (temporary). Which can we do fast?
liam_infra: we can toggle flag via runtime config at the cluster manager; requires a restart of the worker service, ~30s per instance. But safe to do as a staged ramp.
mike_eng: runtime has a hidden env RUN_COMPILE_DEFER=0 that forces old compile path. I can push a config change to 10% of serving pool now. command: ```
# deploy config to 10% of pool
redwoodctl rollout --cluster prod-us-west --env RUN_COMPILE_DEFER=0 --percent 10
```
ava_oncall: do it. watch p95/p99 and streaming timeouts. @sofia_support notify cust-zenith we're rolling mitigations and may route them to eu as fallback.
sofia_support: notified, they requested ETA for full restoration. I'll update them: "we're rolling a runtime config to reduce compile-path regressions; expected impact within 10-15 minutes".
mike_eng: rollout started. initial 10% nodes show p99 drop from 2.7s -> 1.4s. good sign. amplifying to 50%.
liam_infra: scaling rollback plan in parallel: creating node replacement job to restore v4.19-stable kernel image. ETA ~40-60m for full pool if needed.
rachel_runtime: enabling prefix caching for affected model families would help but risk memory bump; need safety check. can enable on 25% now if needed.
dario_sre: timeline: T+0m alert -> T+2m canary config -> T+8m 50% config -> T+35m node replacements start if needed. Customer impact: p99 partially improved but still borderline for some synthetic-heavy streams.
ava_oncall: monitoring shows stream timeouts dropping to baseline on nodes with config. starting controlled routing away from nodes still on trt8 when % traffic > threshold.
liam_infra: I'm patching the autoscaler to avoid placing new pods on trt8 nodes while replacement job runs. updated policy: prefer stable nodes.
sofia_support: cust-zenith accepts routing to eu for now, but wants a postmortem and root cause once stable. assigning follow-up to @rachel_runtime and @liam_infra.
mike_eng: pushed 50% config, p99 on 50% nodes at 1.2s. aggregate p99 down to 1.5s. still above some SLOs but trending.
ava_oncall: ok continue ramp to 100% config. keep rollback job running as fallback. if p99 stops improving after 100% then we do full kernel image rollback.
rachel_runtime: note for postmortem: capture compile artifacts, kernel vm tunables, and exact flashattn kernel build flags. also collect perf top on affected decode path.
dario_sre: incident severity: stay at sev2 until p99 <1.2s and cust-zenith confirms normal.
ava_oncall: escalation & handoff: I'll stay on for next 30m while we finish rollouts. After that, @liam_infra will take over monitoring and kernel replacements; @rachel_runtime owns root cause and postmortem.
sofia_support: queued a follow-up call with cust-zenith in 1hr. they want any remediation steps and confirmation before midday.
liam_infra: final notes before handoff: node-replace job started, ~15% replaced so far. no data-plane errors seen from replacement.
ava_oncall: thanks all. summarizing for handoff -> next shift: current mitigation = RUN_COMPILE_DEFER=0 rolled to 100% (expected soon), kernel replacement in progress (v4.19-stable), watchlist = decode.p99, streaming.timeout.count, node vmstat pgpgin/pgpgout.
ava_oncall: handing off at 2753012699 to @liam_infra for live watch. I'll post incident timeline + resources in #incidents after wrap. :white_check_mark:
liam_infra: acknowledged. taking over watch. will ping if any regressions.
sofia_support: noted. updating customer.
incident-bot: [RESOLVE-IF] p99 decode < 1.2s sustained for 10m -> consider closing paging alert.
